plan.planning_summary: Refining route_02 (24-layer HfO2/SiO2 dichroic stack) based on iteration_12 results showing best_target_score = 0.907. Three complementary routes explore: (1) localized smoothing constraint on the reactive transition block layers 12-15 per feedback directive, (2) expanded 26-layer topology to test if additional degrees of freedom improve spectral separation, (3) reduced 22-layer topology to test if simpler stack achieves comparable performance with better manufacturability. All routes preserve the proven alternating HfO2/SiO2 topology and dual-band objective.

routes.title: Transition-Block Smoothed 24-Layer Dichroic Stack
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Applying localized smoothing constraints to the highly reactive transition block (layers 12-15) will reduce oscillatory overshooting while preserving the beneficial non-uniform topology discovered in iteration_12, leading to improved convergence stability and potentially higher best_target_score.
routes.design_principle: Gradient-based thickness optimization with bounded step-size modulation on layers 12-15 to prevent abrupt thickness changes that cause spectral oscillations, while allowing full search bounds on outer layers.
routes.proposed_topology: 24-layer alternating stack starting with HfO2 on air side, ending with SiO2 on fused silica substrate side. Exact sequence: HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2
design_variables: All 24 layer thicknesses with layers 12-15 constrained to +/-10% change per optimization step
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band
Maximize mean reflectance in 400-700 nm band
Maintain smooth thickness progression in transition block
manufacturing_considerations: Thickness bounds 50-280 nm for all layers
Localized smoothing may improve deposition uniformity in transition region
theory_basis: Thin-film interference theory for dual-band dichroic filters
Transfer-matrix method for coherent multilayer stacks
Gradient-based optimization with localized constraints for stability
expected_advantages: Reduced risk of local minima trapping in transition region
Potentially higher best_target_score than iteration_12 baseline
known_risks: Over-constraining layers 12-15 may prevent discovery of optimal thickness configuration
Smoothing constraint may limit exploration of beneficial non-uniform topologies
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 24-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 dichroic stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence at normal angle. Initialize thicknesses from iteration_12 best candidate: [77.71, 177.76, 65.96, 87.63, 94.31, 100.73, 236.5, 85.64, 126.52, 87.8, 60.22, 87.68, 209.35, 88.73, 63.43, 79.31, 63.65, 84.16, 163.16, 212.54, 63.22, 82.93, 177.9, 68.43] nm. Apply gradient-based thickness optimization with bounds 50-280 nm for all layers. Impose localized smoothing constraint on layers 12-15 (indices 11-14 zero-based) limiting thickness change to +/-10% per optimization step. Evaluate coherent TMM at normal incidence unpolarized. Score candidates by mean transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band and mean reflectance in 400-700 nm band with equal weighting. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 1530-1565 nm, 400-700 nm. soft objectives: High transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band; High reflectance in 400-700 nm band. behaviors to suppress or avoid: Low reflectance in 1530-1565 nm band; Low transmittance in 400-700 nm band. manufacturing constraints: Total layer count <= 30.
routes.revision_reason: Applied feedback directive to restrict step size on highly reactive transition block layers 12-15 to prevent oscillatory overshooting while preserving beneficial non-uniform topology from iteration_12.

routes.title: Expanded 26-Layer Dichroic Stack with Additional Degrees of Freedom
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Increasing layer count from 24 to 26 within the 30-layer manufacturing limit will provide additional degrees of freedom for spectral shaping, potentially improving the dual-band separation performance beyond iteration_12 results.
routes.design_principle: Extend the proven 24-layer alternating topology by adding one HfO2/SiO2 pair in the middle transition region where spectral shaping is most critical, then optimize all thicknesses.
routes.proposed_topology: 26-layer alternating stack starting with HfO2 on air side, ending with SiO2 on fused silica substrate side. Exact sequence: HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band
Maximize mean reflectance in 400-700 nm band
manufacturing_considerations: Thickness bounds 50-280 nm for all layers
Two additional layers increase deposition time but remain within constraint
theory_basis: Thin-film interference theory: additional layers increase spectral degrees of freedom
Transfer-matrix method for coherent multilayer stacks
Dichroic filter design principle: more layers enable sharper band edges
expected_advantages: Potentially higher best_target_score due to increased design freedom
Sharper spectral transition between pass and stop bands
Better ability to suppress visible band while maintaining IR transmission
known_risks: Additional layers increase manufacturing complexity and cost
May not yield significant improvement if 24-layer already near optimal
Risk of overfitting to specific wavelength points rather than bands
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 26-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 dichroic stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence at normal angle. Initialize thicknesses by interpolating iteration_12 best candidate 24-layer thicknesses across 26 layers, with two additional layers inserted at positions 12-13 (zero-based indices) initialized to 100 nm each. Apply gradient-based thickness optimization with bounds 50-280 nm for all 26 layers. Evaluate coherent TMM at normal incidence unpolarized. Score candidates by mean transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band and mean reflectance in 400-700 nm band with equal weighting. Total layer count fixed at 26. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 1530-1565 nm, 400-700 nm. soft objectives: High transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band; High reflectance in 400-700 nm band. behaviors to suppress or avoid: Low reflectance in 1530-1565 nm band; Low transmittance in 400-700 nm band. manufacturing constraints: Total layer count <= 30.
routes.revision_reason: Explores whether additional layers beyond the proven 24-layer topology can improve dual-band performance while remaining within 30-layer manufacturing constraint.

routes.title: Reduced 22-Layer Dichroic Stack for Manufacturability
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Reducing layer count from 24 to 22 will simplify manufacturing while maintaining acceptable dual-band performance, testing whether the 24-layer topology has redundant layers that do not contribute significantly to spectral separation.
routes.design_principle: Remove one HfO2/SiO2 pair from the 24-layer topology at a position with minimal spectral impact (based on iteration_12 thickness sensitivity), then re-optimize remaining 22 layers.
routes.proposed_topology: 22-layer alternating stack starting with HfO2 on air side, ending with SiO2 on fused silica substrate side. Exact sequence: HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band
Maximize mean reflectance in 400-700 nm band
manufacturing_considerations: Total layer count = 22 (within 30-layer limit, reduced from 24)
Thickness bounds 50-280 nm for all layers
Fewer layers reduce deposition time and potential cumulative error
theory_basis: Thin-film interference theory: minimum layer count for dual-band separation
Transfer-matrix method for coherent multilayer stacks
Manufacturing constraint optimization: fewer layers reduce cost and error accumulation
expected_advantages: Potentially comparable performance if 24-layer had redundant layers
known_risks: best_target_score may decrease if 22 layers insufficient for spectral separation
May not achieve iteration_12 performance levels
Reduced design freedom may limit optimization convergence
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 22-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 dichroic stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence at normal angle. Initialize thicknesses by removing layers at positions 10-11 (zero-based indices) from iteration_12 best candidate 24-layer thicknesses, resulting in 22 thickness values. Apply gradient-based thickness optimization with bounds 50-280 nm for all 22 layers. Evaluate coherent TMM at normal incidence unpolarized. Score candidates by mean transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band and mean reflectance in 400-700 nm band with equal weighting. Total layer count fixed at 22. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 1530-1565 nm, 400-700 nm. soft objectives: High transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band; High reflectance in 400-700 nm band. behaviors to suppress or avoid: Low reflectance in 1530-1565 nm band; Low transmittance in 400-700 nm band. manufacturing constraints: Total layer count <= 30.
routes.revision_reason: Tests whether reduced layer count can maintain acceptable performance while improving manufacturability, complementary to the 26-layer expansion route.

research_influence: Evidence ID s2-chunk:CorpusId:92993850:s2chunk:92993850:1765:3736:69b2ad685bc8c493 confirms telecom C-band (1550 nm) importance for satellite quantum communication, motivating the high-priority treatment of 1530-1565 nm transmission objective. No literature evidence directly supports dichroic filter design methodology, so all routes rely on theory_basis for optical design principles.
unresolved_decisions: Optimal layer count between 22-26 layers remains unknown - these three routes will provide comparative evidence
Whether localized smoothing on layers 12-15 improves convergence versus full unconstrained optimization requires experimental validation
Trade-off between performance (best_target_score) and manufacturability (layer count) not yet quantified
plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: Stop after the bounded route portfolio is exhausted or further search stagnates. Return every physically verified candidate and report soft objective trade-offs without a performance admission threshold.
